_about: The rule documents a repair and a claim cite (rules/repair.py). A construct cannot heal
on its own (Bestiary, Construct type: 'Cannot heal damage on its own, but often can be
repaired ... through the use of the Craft Construct feat. Constructs can also be healed
through spells such as make whole.'), so the hit points a mended machine gets back are
a row's dice, rolled by the engine and stamped rule:<id> — never a number the plan wrote.
THE OWNER'S HOUSE RULE (2026-10-01), verbatim from the option they picked: 'Broken, then
fixable and claimable — House rule: a construct at 0 to -10 is broken, not destroyed
(destroyed only past that). Anyone with the skill can mend it with a Craft or Knowledge
(engineering) check, which heals it. A second, harder check rewrites its loyalty so it
becomes yours: it follows you, obeys, and you can name it.'
Every field marked HOUSE departs from the book; each row's `source` is what it departs
from, kept so the departure is visible.

repair-construct.name: repairing a construct
repair-construct.source: Ultimate Magic p.113, Repairing Constructs (aonprd.com/Rules.aspx?ID=979) — what the house rule departs from: 'a crafter can repair a construct with the Craft Construct feat. When repairing a construct, its master spends 100 gp per Hit Die of the construct, and then makes a skill check as if he were crafting the construct with a DC of 5 less than the DC for crafting that construct. With a success, the construct regains 1d6 hit points per Hit Die of the construct. Completing a repair takes 1 day per 1,000 gp spent on the repair (minimum of 1 day).' And the Bestiary: a construct is 'immediately destroyed when reduced to 0 hit points or less', and 'a construct that has been completely destroyed cannot be repaired'.
repair-construct.house: HOUSE (owner 2026-10-01): no feat and no coin — 'Anyone with the skill can mend it with a Craft or Knowledge (engineering) check, which heals it.' A broken construct (0 to -10) can be mended; only one destroyed past -10 cannot.
repair-construct.skills_house: HOUSE: the better of Craft and Knowledge (engineering) the mender can attempt. The sheet carries one Craft skill, so Craft (clockwork), Craft (weapons) and the rest are all it.
repair-construct.crafting_dc_house: HOUSE, used only when the stat block prints no construction DC: the Core Rulebook's Craft table puts a 'complex or superior item (lock)' at DC 20, so the repair DC is 15. The Clockwork Spy's own printed construction line is Craft (clockwork) DC 20 (Bestiary 3), so for it this is the book's number.
repair-construct.minutes_house: HOUSE: ten minutes an attempt, in place of the book's day per 1,000 gp.
repair-construct.bad_failure_house: HOUSE: a failure by 5 or more is an hour gone, not ten minutes — the work came apart and had to be laid out again. Nothing else is lost and nothing is damaged further.
repair-construct.broken_house: HOUSE: 'a construct at 0 to -10 is broken, not destroyed (destroyed only past that).' broken_floor is the lowest broken total; -11 destroys. The book destroys it at 0.

claim-construct.name: rewriting a construct's loyalty
claim-construct.source: No book rule: a construct obeys its creator (Craft Construct, 'A construct recognizes its creator intuitively and obeys all commands issued to it by that individual'), and the only way to take one from its master is control construct (Ultimate Magic, sorcerer/wizard 7: 'You wrest the control of a construct from its master. For as long as you concentrate, you can control the construct as if you were its master.'). This row is what the house rule puts in its place.
claim-construct.house: HOUSE (owner 2026-10-01): 'A second, harder check rewrites its loyalty so it becomes yours: it follows you, obeys, and you can name it.' Only on a working construct that is not fighting you.
claim-construct.skills_house: HOUSE: the better of Knowledge (engineering) and Disable Device the claimant can attempt. Both are trained-only in 1e.
claim-construct.dc_house: HOUSE: the construct's repair DC plus 10 — 25 for the Clockwork Spy.
claim-construct.attitude_house: HOUSE: it becomes yours — bond.owned-by-you, bond.travels-with-you (it follows), and the top of the attitude track, devoted (it obeys).
claim-construct.bad_failure_house: HOUSE: a failure by 5 or more and the machine fights the rewrite — it turns hostile.
